Subject: Kickoff & network checklist for Praxis on-prem deployment

Hi Sergio / Monica,

Thanks for the onboarding call earlier — we wanted to capture the immediate networking asks so we can schedule our infra team for a dedicated review. Attached is our current VPC CIDR list and a quick spreadsheet with topology notes. High level asks:

- We need VPC peering between our primary AWS account (10.10.0.0/16) and Redwood's private endpoints.
- Support for private S3 access (VPC endpoint) and ability to restrict egress to our proxy.
- We are evaluating an air-gapped on-prem package for a subset of workloads; need specifics on package size and OS requirements.

Can someone from your side send a checklist of exact ports, NAT/route table expectations, and whether a bastion host is required for the initial install? Also please advise on KMS/HSM key policy requirements for customer-managed keys.

I've attached: praxis-current-cidr.csv and praxis-network-requirements.xlsx. Arjun (cc) will be our infra PM and will join the network review.

Thanks,
Priya Menon

Subject: Re: Kickoff & network checklist for Praxis on-prem deployment

Priya — thanks for the details and the CIDR file. We can run a short 60-minute network review next week to go over VPC peering, private endpoints, and the on-prem package constraints.

Attached is our internal "Redwood private deploy network checklist v1.3" (see rdw-onprem-v1.3.tar.gz stub) which covers the minimum:

- Required outbound ports: 443 (control plane), 2379/2380 (etcd, if using HA on-prem), 22 (optional, bastion only), 9000-9100 (internal gRPC between nodes)
- IPs to reserve: list of recommended /28 for each node pool and a /27 for management traffic
- Route behavior: prefer explicit route propagation disabled; use static peering routes from customer to Redwood endpoints
- S3: VPC endpoint + policy to allow specific bucket ARNs; recommend VPC endpoint policy limit
- KMS: customer-managed key ok; we need Key ARN and a policy allowing the Redwood inference service principal to Encrypt/Decrypt

Quick asks before the call:
1) Confirm the /16 you sent (10.10.0.0/16) — any overlapping on-prem ranges?
2) Do you require a fully air-gapped install (no egress) or a restricted egress via a proxy/NAT?
3) Which OS for on-prem nodes (RHEL 8 / Ubuntu 22.04 recommended)?

Proposed times for the network review: Tue 11/2 09:00-10:00 PT or Wed 11/3 14:00-15:00 PT. I'll invite our solutions engineer (Prio) and Monica (CS lead).

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Customer Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: Kickoff & network checklist for Praxis on-prem deployment — technical notes

Hi all,

Adding a few technical specifics ahead of the call so your infra team can validate:

Network & routing
- We support two integration patterns: (A) Cross-account VPC peering to our private endpoints (recommended for low latency) or (B) PrivateLink endpoints in your account referencing our NLB (better isolation, slightly higher cost).
- For peering (A): we need static routes in your route tables pointing to Redwood's peering attachment for the subnets used by inference nodes. Avoid overlapping CIDRs (no /16 overlap).
- MTU: set to 9001 if you enable jumbo frames — avoids issues with gRPC payloads.

Ports & security groups
- Control Plane: outbound 443 to control.redwood.example (TLS).
- Inter-node: TCP 9000-9100 (intra-cluster gRPC); allow only from peer subnets.
- Admin: SSH (22) only to bastion host with IP whitelist.

Storage & S3
- If you want private S3: create a VPC endpoint with policy limiting access to the buckets listed in your sheet. We can provide bucket ARNs on request.
- For air-gapped installs: we provide an OCI-formatted image tarball (rdw-onprem-v1.3.tar.gz) and a package manifest. You will need an internal registry (Harbor/Artifactory) and package checksum verification.

KMS & certs
- Provide the KMS key ARN. We require an IAM role + key policy allowing the Redwood service principal: arn:aws:iam::redwood:role/inference-service (we'll send the exact ARN). For HSM/FIPS requests, note additional lead time for validation (2-3 weeks).

Can you confirm the CIDR block for your management VLAN and if you have a prioritized maintenance window for initial install?

— Priyom
Sr Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai

Thanks Priyom — this is very helpful. A few answers below and one ask: can you send a trimmed manifest we can give our security team for an air-gapped install?

- CIDR confirmation: Primary AWS VPC 10.10.0.0/16 (no known overlaps). Management VLANs: 10.200.0.0/24.
- We will require an air-gapped package for our clinical environment (no outbound internet except to our patch proxy). For the rest of the cluster (non-clinical), we can allow outbound via a corporate NAT.
- OS: we run RHEL 8.6 for both hosts.
- Maintenance window: prefer weekend (Sat 11/13 00:00-06:00 PT) for the initial install.

- Deployment model: hybrid — air-gapped package for clinical cluster + internet-enabled non-clinical cluster.
- OS: RHEL 8.6.
- Target install window: Sat 2026-11-13 00:00-06:00 PT.

Action items (owner / ETA)

- Praxis (Arjun): Share management VLAN contacts and confirm bastion IP allowlist by 2026-11-04. (arjun@praxis-med.com)

Network review meeting: Confirmed Tue 2026-11-02 09:00 PT (calendar invite sent). Please come with access to your network team and any firewall diagrams.

Notes / risks
- If HSM/FIPS validation is required, expect 2–3 week additional lead time; flag now if this is a hard requirement.
- Air-gapped installs will require an internal registry + checksum verification and slightly longer validation tests — plan for a 2-day validation run post-install.

I'll follow up with the MAP and a short checklist PDF. Thanks everyone — looking forward to the review.

Best,
